text:
**For most people, LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice.** Nearly every current power station uses it, so you usually don't have to choose.

**Where LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** This is the biggest difference. Rated cycles are typically 3,000 to 6,000 for LFP and 500 to 1,000 for NMC. At one full cycle a day, that's roughly 8+ years versus under 2 years ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).
- **Failure behavior:** In lab tests, LFP cells burned cooler and less violently than NMC when they failed. In one test, LFP peaked at 259°C versus 731°C for NMC ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)). LFP isn't fireproof, but this matters if you keep the unit indoors or in a vehicle.
- **Cost over time:** Price per watt-hour is now similar. One database shows a median of $0.55/Wh for LFP versus $0.95/Wh for NMC ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Per rated cycle, LFP is much cheaper.

**Where NMC wins**
- **Energy density:** NMC cells hold more energy per pound. In finished stations the gap is much smaller, about 10% in one database, and some LFP models are lighter per watt-hour than some NMC ones ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)). Compare actual specs rather than assuming the chemistry decides weight.

**Cold weather is mostly a tie.** Sources disagree here. Several say both chemistries refuse to charge below 32°F, and that the limits depend on the maker more than the chemistry ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)). Check the manual's charging range if you'll use it in winter.

**Read cycle ratings carefully.** "3,000 cycles to 80%" is a stronger promise than "4,000 cycles to 70%." Test conditions also vary by brand.

**Quick guide**
- **Daily or frequent use (van, off-grid, solar):** LiFePO4.
- **Home outage backup:** LiFePO4, though NMC's cycle count would also last for rare use.
- **Weight is critical, or you only use it a few weekends a year:** Either, chosen on specific specs and price.
- **Already own a working NMC unit:** Keep using it.

**One example:** The [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2) is a 2,073.6 Wh LiFePO4 station rated for 6,000+ cycles to 80%. It has a 2,600 W inverter, a 5-year warranty, and weighs 24.2 kg (about 53 lb). It's $899 at BLUETTI, or $854.05 with code AFF5OFF according to the listing ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-elite-200-v2)). It isn't expandable.
